Whittaker-Henderson smoother with GCV

Source: R/smoothers.R
whittaker_smooth.Rd

Penalised least-squares smoother: solves \((W + \lambda D'D) z = W y\), with D the difference matrix of a given order, and chooses \(\lambda\) by generalised cross-validation.

Usage

whittaker_smooth(
  y,
  lambda = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  order = 2L,
  log10_grid = seq(0, 9, 0.1)
)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector; NA allowed (weight zero).

lambda

NULL (choose by GCV) or a single positive smoothing parameter.

weights

NULL (all ones) or non-negative weights of the same length as y.

order

Order of the differences in the penalty (positive integer, default 2).

log10_grid

Grid of \(\log_{10}\lambda\) values searched when lambda = NULL.

Value

A list with trend (numeric, same length as y), lambda (used), edf (equivalent degrees of freedom), gcv (GCV at lambda) and path (data.table with lambda, edf and gcv over the grid; one row when lambda is given).

Details

Missing values and weights. NA values of y get weight zero: the smoother interpolates them (a polynomial spline of degree 2 * order - 1 between observed points). A weight of zero and an NA give the same result.

Limits. As \(\lambda \to 0\) the solution tends to y (at points with positive weight); as \(\lambda \to \infty\) it tends to the weighted least-squares polynomial of degree order - 1 (a straight line for order = 2, which is the Hodrick-Prescott filter). For weekly series the Ravn-Uhlig rule gives \(\lambda = 1600 \cdot 13^4\), about \(10^{7.66}\), for comparison with the GCV choice.

GCV. For each \(\lambda = 10^g\), g in log10_grid, \(GCV = m\,RSS_w / (m - \mathrm{edf})^2\), with m the number of positive weights, \(RSS_w = \sum w_i (y_i - z_i)^2\) and \(\mathrm{edf} = \mathrm{tr}[(W + \lambda D'D)^{-1} W]\). The system is solved with sparse matrices (Matrix); the trace is exact, from the dense inverse of the Cholesky factor, which costs \(O(n^3)\) per grid value: fine for a few hundred weeks, slow for many thousands of points. GCV assumes independent errors and tends to undersmooth under positive autocorrelation.

References

Eilers, P. H. C. (2003). A perfect smoother. Analytical Chemistry, 75(14), 3631-3636.

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- cumsum(rnorm(150, 0, 0.1)) + rnorm(150, 0, 0.3)
y[c(20, 21, 90)] <- NA
wh <- whittaker_smooth(y)
log10(wh$lambda)
#> [1] 3
wh$edf
#> [1] 10.41281
# Ravn-Uhlig value for weekly data
whittaker_smooth(y, lambda = 1600 * 13^4)$edf
#> [1] 2.02552
